questions: How many nano-SQUID devices did you measure in total, including those where only the Josephson junctions worked, and how many showed the Ic oscillations, the diode sign reversal and zero-bias peaks? The paper names devices A, B and C and says the global signatures appear "in all examined devices" (p. 4).
Why were the other devices set aside, in particular the rest of the "series of devices with two functioning tunnel contacts" (p. 4), and what did they show?
Which ranges did you measure beyond the ones shown: temperatures above the 30 mK base, field angles away from the nanowire axis, and, for device A, gate voltages outside -10 to 20 V?

What does the second-best dataset look like? Device C answers this in part (pp. 12-13); is there a second case like Fig. 1f, where a zero-bias peak appears at half-integer flux and persists over a wide field range?

Would a trivial two-junction interferometer model, with skewed current-phase relations and unequal JJ1 and JJ2 transparencies fitted to your data, reproduce Ic(Φ) and η(Φ) in Figs. 1e, 3a and S2a, and which features would it miss?
What are the transparencies of JJ1 and JJ2 (for example from the excess current, or IcRN in Fig. 4j), and how do they change with VG?

For the end-to-end correlation in Fig. 4l and Fig. S3l, which smoothing, derivative step and bias window did you use, how did you classify points where neither end shows a clear peak or dip, and how do the fractions change when you vary these choices?

At zero field, do the tunnel spectra show Coulomb diamonds or resonances above the gap, or zero-bias peaks that alternate between gate-voltage windows, and how do the zero-field peaks depend on temperature?
